title: 2024 budget directions and downtown development approvals
subtitle: Zoning approvals in Elora and Fergus, parking by-law, termite management, short-term rentals, advisory committees and Elora Rapids access.
overview: Council set early direction for the 2024 budget. Staff are to aim for a tax rate increase of 6.0% or less, with recommendations for reaching 4.5%. That figure includes dedicated increases of 2% for asset management and 1% for termite management {{vote:m5}}. Fees and charges are to rise 6.0% in general, and assessment growth is assumed at 2.5%. Final budget approval is expected in December.

Council approved zoning amendments for mixed-use buildings at 175-183 Geddes Street in Elora {{vote:m15}} and 350 St. Andrew Street West in Fergus {{vote:m17}}. It also adopted a new parking by-law {{vote:m21}}, a mandatory pre-consultation by-law for planning applications {{vote:m29}}, and weekly downtown waste collection in Fergus and Elora {{vote:m18}}.

Other decisions included a parking strategy contract, Moir Street reconstruction, extra funding for Bridge 3N repairs, a Commercial Access Agreement with Elora Rapids, and a vendor-run Sportsplex concession. Council also asked staff to report on short-term rental management, with a program targeted for May 1, 2024 {{vote:m37}}, and set up its advisory committees.

decisions.detail: Staff were directed to prepare a 2024 draft budget with a tax rate increase of 6.0% or less, including recommendations to achieve 4.5%.
Staff will include an increase equivalent to 1% in taxation in the 2024 draft budget to fund the termite management program.
Council approved the zoning amendment for 175-183 Geddes Street and gave the by-law three readings.

decisions.item: St. Andrew Street West rezoning, Fergus
decisions.detail: Council approved the zoning amendment for 350 St. Andrew St. W. and gave the by-law three readings.
The Mayor and Clerk may sign an agreement with the County of Wellington for weekly waste collection in downtown Fergus and Elora.
Council authorized execution of By-law 6000-23, regulating parking and stopping on highways, public lots and private property.
The Mayor and Clerk may sign a Commercial Access Agreement for Elora Rapids use of Blair Park and Elora Community Centre property.
Staff will research best practices and report back so a short-term rental program can be in place by May 1, 2024.
